gloss: only one person; all alone; just one person

definitions.gloss: only one person; all alone; just one person
definitions.explanation: Emphasizes that there is just a single person, often conveying loneliness, uniqueness, or the surprising smallness of the number.

examples.japanese: たった{一人|ひとり}で{暮|く}らしている。
{合格|ごうかく}したのはたった{一人|ひとり}だけだった。
たった{一人|ひとり}の{家族|かぞく}を{失|うしな}った{悲|かな}しみは{計|はか}り{知|し}れない。
examples.english: The grief of losing one's only family member is immeasurable.

notes:
A set phrase combining たった ('only, just, merely') with {一人|ひとり} ('one person'). The adverb たった emphasizes how surprisingly or strikingly small the number is. It conveys emotional weight — loneliness, isolation, or the significance of being the sole person.

USAGE:
たった can combine with other counters and numbers: たった{一|ひと}つ ('just one thing'), たった{二人|ふたり} ('only two people'), たった{三日|みっか} ('a mere three days').

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ひとりぼっち: all alone — emphasizes the loneliness of being by oneself
- {唯一|ゆいいつ}の: the only, sole — more formal; used as a modifier
- たった{一|ひと}つ: just one (thing) — the same pattern with a different counter
